content: The Global Accelerated Action for the Health of Adolescents (AA-HA.) guidance, second edition, is a comprehensive document designed to support countries in implementing strategies to improve adolescent health and well-being. Published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2023, it builds on the first edition released in 2017 and incorporates lessons learned, updated data, and new frameworks to address the evolving needs of adolescents globally. The document emphasizes the importance of investing in adolescent health, highlighting the unique developmental stage of adolescence and its potential to yield a triple dividend of benefits: improving the health of adolescents now, enhancing their future adult lives, and positively impacting the next generation. It integrates the latest evidence on health, mortality, morbidity, and well-being determinants, while also reflecting on the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic. The guidance underscores the need for a multisectoral approach, involving collaboration across health, education, nutrition, and social systems. It advocates for evidence-based, holistic interventions that address the interconnectedness of health, education, life skills, and employability. The document also highlights the critical role of adolescents and youth as co-creators in designing and delivering policies and programs that affect their lives, ensuring their voices are heard and respected. The second edition incorporates the Adolescent Well-Being Framework, developed in partnership with PMNCH (Partnership for Maternal, Newborn & Child Health) and UN agencies, to guide programming and policy development. It also aligns with global initiatives such as the Education Plus program, which aims to empower girls through secondary education, life skills, and access to health services, particularly in Africa. The foreword by Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General, emphasizes the urgency of advancing adolescent health to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and create a healthier, more equitable future. Contributions from leaders of various UN agencies, including UNAIDS, UNESCO, UNFPA, UNICEF, UN Women, and WFP, highlight the collaborative effort to address the diverse needs of adolescents, from sexual and reproductive health to nutrition and education. The guidance also stresses the importance of addressing inequalities that prevent adolescents from accessing essential health services, including HIV services, and calls for youth-led, multisystem approaches to ensure equitable and comprehensive care. It recognizes the transformative potential of empowering young women and girls, promoting gender equality, and fostering leadership through mentorship and engagement. The document concludes with a call to action for governments, organizations, and stakeholders to prioritize adolescent health and well-being, leveraging the updated guidance as a roadmap for transformative change. By investing in adolescents today, the global community can build a foundation for healthier, more empowered future generations.
